stem: A bond's key-rate 01s per 100 face are 0.012 (2-year), 0.031 (5-year), 0.045 (10-year) and 0.020 (30-year). Its DV01 for a parallel shift of the curve is closest to:
explanation: Key-rate shifts add up to a parallel shift, so DV01 ≈ 0.012 + 0.031 + 0.045 + 0.020 = 0.108.

rationale.A: Incorrect. 0.045 is only the largest single key-rate exposure, not the total parallel sensitivity.
rationale.B: Correct. Summing the key-rate 01s gives the parallel-shift DV01 of 0.108.
rationale.C: Incorrect. 0.027 is the average key-rate 01; the exposures add rather than average.
rationale.D: Incorrect. 0.088 leaves out the 30-year key-rate exposure.

stem: Key rates are set at 2, 5, 10 and 30 years. If the 5-year key rate rises by 10 basis points and all other key rates are unchanged, the 7-year spot rate rises by approximately:
explanation: The shift falls linearly from 10 bp at 5 years to 0 at 10 years: 10 × (10 − 7)/(10 − 5) = 6 bp.

rationale.A: Incorrect. The full 10 bp applies only at the 5-year key rate itself, not between key rates.
rationale.B: Incorrect. 4 bp uses (7 − 5)/(10 − 5), giving the weight of the 10-year key rate rather than the 5-year one.
rationale.C: Incorrect. Maturities between key rates are affected by both neighbouring key rates through linear interpolation.
rationale.D: Correct. Linear interpolation gives 10 × 3/5 = 6 bp at 7 years.

stem: A portfolio has key-rate 01s of USD 4,000 per bp at 5 years and USD 9,000 per bp at 10 years. Hedge bonds have the following key-rate 01s per USD 1 million face: the 10-year bond has USD 20 (5-year) and USD 850 (10-year); the 5-year bond has USD 450 (5-year) and 0 (10-year). The face amount of the 5-year bond to sell is closest to:
explanation: First the 10-year key rate: F10 = 9,000 / 850 = 10.588 million. It covers 10.588 × 20 = 211.76 of 5-year exposure, leaving 4,000 − 211.76 = 3,788.24. F5 = 3,788.24 / 450 = USD 8.42 million.

rationale.A: Correct. After the 10-year hedge absorbs 211.76 of 5-year exposure, the 5-year bond must cover 3,788.24 / 450 = USD 8.42 million.
rationale.B: Incorrect. USD 8.89 million (4,000 / 450) ignores the 5-year exposure already hedged by the 10-year bond.
rationale.C: Incorrect. USD 10.59 million is the face amount of the 10-year bond, not the 5-year bond.
rationale.D: Incorrect. USD 9.36 million adds the 10-year bond's 5-year exposure instead of subtracting it.

stem: A swap desk builds its curve from quoted par swap rates. To report risk in instruments it can trade directly, it bumps each quoted swap rate by 1 basis point in turn, rebuilds the curve with the other quotes unchanged, and reprices the book. This measure is best described as:
options: Key-rate durations based on spot rates
explanation: Partial 01s measure sensitivity to each par instrument used to build the curve: bump one quote, rebuild, reprice. This links risk directly to hedging instruments.

rationale.A: Incorrect. Forward-bucket 01s shift all forward rates within a maturity bucket, not individual par quotes.
rationale.B: Incorrect. Effective duration measures the response to a single parallel shift, not to each instrument separately.
rationale.C: Correct. Bumping each curve-building par quote and rebuilding the curve produces partial 01s.
rationale.D: Incorrect. Key-rate durations shift chosen spot or par yields with linear fading between key rates, rather than rebuilding the curve from each market quote.
